title: A Retrospective Analysis of the Agreement Between the Preliminary Diagnoses of Patients Presented to the Emergency Medical Service—Who Were Treated by Paramedics from the Emergency Medical Service of the State Capital of Düsseldorf—and the Clinical Diagnoses Made by the Emergency Department of the University Hospital of Düsseldorf
summary:
The study is being conducted retrospectively at the Emergency Department of the University Hospital of Düsseldorf. Only data that was already collected as part of routine patient care is being analyzed. No additional examinations, interviews, or contact with patients is taking place.

For the analysis, data from the emergency medical services and the Emergency Department are being compared. The prehospital data comes from the medDV-NIDAclient documentation system. Among other things, this system records the suspected diagnosis, the patient’s age, the urgency level, and the date and time of the emergency medical service call. Some of this information is mapped via the patient referral code (PZC) from IVENA.

The study includes all eligible patients who were presented to the Emergency Department of the University Hospital Düsseldorf by paramedics from the emergency medical services of the State Capital of Düsseldorf between August 1, 2025, and November 30, 2025. Approximately 300 eligible cases per month are expected.

Data from the emergency medical services will be merged with existing routine clinical data from the hospital information systems COPRA and MEDICO. In particular, the following information will be recorded: the date and time of admission, age, urgency classification according to the Manchester Triage System, the final primary clinical diagnosis, and the patient’s subsequent disposition.

The clinical reference diagnosis is defined as the primary diagnosis documented for the respective reason for presentation after treatment was completed in the Emergency Department. Before the analysis begins, a uniform decision is made regarding which data source will be used for this purpose and how to proceed when multiple diagnoses have been documented.

The goal is to examine how well the suspected diagnosis made by the emergency medical services corresponds to the clinical diagnosis subsequently established in the Emergency Department.
conditions: Patients from the emergency medical services who were transported to an emergency department by emergency medical personnel

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-    Treatment at the Emergency Department of the University Hospital of Düsseldorf between August 1, 2025, and November 30, 2025.
-    Transport by an ambulance from the emergency medical services of the State Capital of Düsseldorf.
-    Prehospital care provided by emergency medical technicians without the involvement of an emergency physician.
-    Availability of an assignable prehospital data record and the routine clinical data required for the endpoint analysis.
Exclusion criteria:
-    Reports of incidents involving emergency medical personnel
-    Ambulance records
-    Missing prehospital reporting indicator (RMI/PZC) or clinical reference diagnosis (from the Emergency Department) required for analysis of the primary endpoint
-    Unassignable data records
-    Records of secondary transfers between medical facilities
